in_text_mentions: While these methods allowed for some improvement in the wounds as visualized above, the patient unfortunately returned to the hospital with worsening wounds in late spring 2025. The above wounds were noted to have new nodules with seropurulent drainage, and necrotic eschar was visualized on both the anterior tibia and posterior calf (Figure 6). The anterior tibial lesion was excised down to the ulcer bed, and final pathology resulted in the diagnosis of NL.

A: Panel-specific caption describes anterior tibial erythematous nodules with ulceration in article titled Necrobiosis Lipoidica Mimicking Chronic Infectious Ulceration, supporting necrobiosis lipoidica attribution. B: Caption describes distal anterior tibial erythematous nodules with seropurulent drainage in necrobiosis lipoidica case, consistent with ulcerated plaque. C: Caption describes large erythematous atrophic nodule on posterior lower limb in necrobiosis lipoidica case; atrophy and erythema support attribution despite non-pretibial location. D: Caption describes posterior atrophic nodules with ulceration and active drainage in necrobiosis lipoidica case, supporting ulcerated disease.
